# WaterRAT

Water Rights Allocation Tool for R (`WaterRAT`) prepares state water-right
points of diversion (PODs), assigns them to the NHDPlus hydrofabric, and routes
authorized allocations through a connected stream network. The review output is
a GIS-ready GeoPackage with allocation, streamflow, and audit fields.

Full setup, filtering, schema, and workflow documentation is available at
<https://soilwaterfish.github.io/WaterRAT/>.

## Installation

```r
remotes::install_github("soilwaterfish/WaterRAT")
```

WaterRAT version-controls code and documentation only. Keep source
geodatabases, NHDPlus, FlowMet, caches, and results in the ignored `data/` or
`dev/` paths. Dataset links and expected local inputs are listed in the
[setup documentation](https://soilwaterfish.github.io/WaterRAT/setup/).

## Two-stage workflow

The workflow deliberately separates state preparation from network analysis.

1. `prep_targets.R` prepares updated state data and stores it in the combined
   `data/cache/prepped/water_rights.gpkg` cache. Idaho filters the POD layer
   first and reuses cached Water Uses report results for unchanged POD
   identity, report URL, status, source, and location. Montana filters to
   eligible August PODs, indexes candidate locations, and retains the
   downstream-most POD for each `WRKEY`. Both first intersect PODs with the
   local NHDPlus `Catchment` layer, using its `FEATUREID` as the COMID. NLDI
   checkpoints under `data/cache/nldi/` are retained only for the rare PODs
   with no single local catchment match.
2. `_targets.R` reads the one prepared multi-state layer and performs network
   accumulation through NHDPlus. It has no water-right scraping step, so it
   can be rerun independently whenever routing, FlowMet, or reporting changes.

```r
# Incrementally refresh Idaho and Montana preparation.
targets::tar_make(script = "prep_targets.R", store = "_targets_prep")

# Route all states contained in the prepared cache as one network.
targets::tar_make()
```

The separate targets stores prevent ordinary network analysis from invalidating
the state-preparation cache. On a future refresh, removed state records are
reported as retired, changed records are re-prepared, and unchanged POD
locations receive local catchment COMIDs without API calls; only unresolved
locations reuse their successful NLDI fallback assignments. Use
`refresh_idwr_network_water_rights(..., force_rescrape = TRUE)` only when IDWR
has changed report-page content without changing the POD layer or report URL.

## State adapters and shared data contract

State adapters bring authoritative source fields into one canonical `sf`
schema. Montana uses `WR_NUMBER` as the water-right ID and `WRKEY` as the site
ID, retaining the most downstream NHDPlus-linked POD where a site has multiple
locations. Idaho uses `WaterRightNumber` as the water-right ID and
`PointOfDiversionID` as the site ID; each qualifying Water Uses row is
standardized and August-overlapping rates are summarized to one site.

Every prepared record includes its canonical allocation fields plus:

* `comid`: local NHDPlus `Catchment$FEATUREID` used for routing (or an NLDI
  fallback result when needed);
* `nldi_error`: explicit explanation when a POD cannot be indexed; and
* `fs_intersection`: Forest Service ownership classification.

See the [filter rules](https://soilwaterfish.github.io/WaterRAT/filters/) and
[canonical schema](https://soilwaterfish.github.io/WaterRAT/schema/) for the
complete crosswalk.

## Local testing and inspection

The package includes paired Montana and Idaho example basins and a clipped
NHDPlus network for function-level inspection. Follow the
[small-scale walkthrough](https://soilwaterfish.github.io/WaterRAT/walkthrough/)
before scaling to a state cache.

```r
devtools::test()
targets::tar_manifest()
targets::tar_manifest(script = "prep_targets.R")
```

The main routing product can be inspected after a successful analysis run:

```r
targets::tar_read(network_allocation)
targets::tar_read(network_allocation_gpkg)
```
